claims.text: The baseline NbMoTaW alloy has a homogeneous disordered microstructure.
Replacing 10–15% of the tungsten with titanium and applying optimized thermal processing will produce a dual-phase microstructure.
The proposed dual-phase microstructure will consist of a disordered matrix containing fine, uniformly distributed, nanometric Ti-induced ordered intermetallic precipitates.
Titanium has a lower atomic mass than tungsten.
Partial replacement of tungsten with titanium will reduce the alloy's density.
Titanium substitution will trigger controlled ordering during thermal processing.
The matrix and precipitates will facilitate load transfer at high temperature.
The ordered intermetallic precipitates will create lattice distortions.
The precipitates will impede high-temperature dislocation motion through mechanisms such as Orowan looping.
Coherent interfaces between the matrix and precipitates will preserve room-temperature ductility.
The modified alloy will exhibit at least a 20% increase in high-temperature yield strength relative to baseline NbMoTaW.
The modified alloy will exhibit at least a 20% improvement in creep resistance relative to baseline NbMoTaW.
The expected high-temperature improvement applies in the 950–1100 °C range under creep and fatigue loading.
Room-temperature tensile strength will deviate by less than 5% from the baseline.
Room-temperature tensile ductility will deviate by less than 5% from the baseline.
Titanium substitution above 15% may cause excessive intermetallic formation.
Excessive intermetallic formation may embrittle the alloy at room temperature.
Titanium substitution below 10% may be insufficient to provide the proposed density reduction or high-temperature strengthening.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome states that both yield strength and creep resistance should improve by at least 20%, whereas the falsification rule refers ambiguously to a 20% improvement in yield strength or creep resistance. This may allow success in only one metric even though the prediction requires both.
